title: Marcus + Asha weekly sync — API/Console/Dedicated/Private prep
content:
Purpose: quick alignment before exec check-in — clear asks from eng + PM, surface risks for Dedicated capacity rollout, confirm console UX changes, and sync on private deployment gating.

Top-line context (2 lines): Hosted API adoption steady; Dedicated pipeline needs final config for autoscale policy; Private deploys pilot (Acme Corp) hitting network/keys friction.

Agenda (30m):
- 5m quick wins / shoutouts (Asha)
- 10m Dedicated capacity: autoscale policy choices, burst config, SLOs (decision needed: default burst threshold)
- 7m Console changes: rollout timing for per-route tracing + cost-breakdown widgets (dependency: PR #489 merged)
- 5m Private: onboarding blocker list for Acme pilot (KMS/HSM handshake, VPC routing)
- 3m parking lot / next steps

Key metrics to share:
- Hosted API 99th latency: 230ms -> target 180ms by end of sprint
- Dedicated utilization: avg 68%, peaks 95% on batch jobs
- Private pilot: 3 failed deploys last week due to cert rotation mismatch

Talking points / prompts for Asha:
- Where are we on autoscaler canary? timeline and rollback plan?
- Risk tolerance for burst capacity (cost vs. SLA) — propose default 25% burst headroom and manual override for enterprise customers.
- Is the tracing widget behind any infra gating (new endpoint, perms)?

Open questions I want answered:
- Can SRE add a granular alert for KV-cache eviction spikes? Who owns that? (Priya?)
- For Private deploys, do we require customers to provide a NAT gateway by default or offer managed egress?

Proposed asks (explicit asks for the meeting):
- Asha: Approve burst default (25%) or give an alternate threshold by EOD Friday.
- Asha + Eng: Confirm canary schedule for autoscaler (start Tue 3/16; rollback windows: 2 hours).
- Evan: Short note on Console UX timeline — can we ship the cost-breakdown in the next minor release?
- Priya: Add KV-cache eviction alert to SRE playbook and link to RED-2241.

Action items (owner, what, by when):
- Marcus: Draft customer-facing note about Dedicated burst behavior (target Wed 3/18).
- Asha: Finalize autoscale canary schedule (by 2026-03-16).
- Priya: Implement eviction alert + runbook (by 2026-03-20).
- Evan: Merge small console wiring PR or flag blockers (by 2026-03-15).

Risk register (short):
- If burst disabled: potential increased throttles for enterprise peak -> customer impact.
- If burst too aggressive: cost exposure. Need middle ground and per-customer overrides.
- Private pilot: cert rotation mismatch could block GA — escalate to platform infra if not fixed in 48h.

Notes template for the meeting (fill during 1:1):
- Decisions made:
- New blockers surfaced:
- Who to escalate to (names + channel):
- Quick wins to communicate to team:

Parking lot / follow-ups (not for blocking this week):
- Explore semi-automated quantization profiles for Dedicated workloads (low priority research spike).
- Draft SLO language for console cost-breakdown (customer-facing).

Quick personal notes to self:
- Keep ask narrow and decision-focused in the meeting. Avoid rehashing old debates about burst economics; present data and recommendation.
- Bring rule-of-thumb cost deltas for 25% vs 50% burst (approx figures).
- If Asha pushes to delay, get concrete alternative timeline and mitigation plan.

Slack refs: #eng-dedicated, #product-console, thread: <slack>/C12AB34/EFG567 — share this doc before sync.

End.
